frontMatter.title: DNS Glossary
frontMatter.description: Definitions of important terms used in DNS

content:
DNS Glossary

Collection of definitions for important terms commonly used in DNS.

A

A Record DNS record that points a domain name to an IPv4 address.

Authoritative Nameserver DNS server that has definitive information about a domain.

C

CNAME Record DNS record that creates an alias or alternative name for another domain.

Cache Temporary storage of DNS query results to speed up subsequent access.

D

DNS Propagation Process of spreading DNS changes to all DNS servers across the internet.

Domain Name Human-readable name to identify internet addresses (example: example.com).

F

FQDN (Fully Qualified Domain Name) Complete domain name that specifies exact location in DNS hierarchy.

M

MX Record DNS record that specifies email server to receive email for a domain.

N

Nameserver Server that stores and manages DNS records for domains.

NS Record DNS record that specifies which nameservers are authoritative for a domain.

R

Recursive Resolver DNS server that performs complete queries to resolve domain names.

Root Domain Highest level in DNS hierarchy, represented by a dot (.).

T

TTL (Time To Live) Time in seconds that determines how long DNS records are stored in cache.

TLD (Top-Level Domain) Top-level domains like .com, .org, .id in DNS hierarchy.

Z

Zone File File containing DNS records for a specific domain.
